name: Mean-variance portfolio effect
title: Is the program book really diversified?
what: Judge how steady a portfolio is against how volatility grows with size, not against the average program.
pick_line: Use the budget-vs-actual gap to strip measurement noise, then refit the size law.
data: SYNTHETIC mock budgets (Corning_mock, MS_mock), not any firm's budget
one: The book is no steadier than one program of the same size.

left.sub: steadier than its programs (average-CV, Corning mock)

right.sub: no steadier than one program that size

findings.h: The book is no steadier than one program of the same size.
findings.t: Usual measures say about 3× steadier. Allowing for how volatility grows with size gives 0.99 (Corning mock) and 1.15 (MS mock).

chart.title: How much steadier is the book?

findings.h: Part of the apparent diversification is measurement noise.
findings.t: On the mocks' noise-free true levels the average-CV effect falls from 3.36 to 1.54 (Corning mock).

findings.h: Honest miss: a plain correlation check finds hidden groups better.
findings.t: Correlation puts all 9 planted groups at the 100th percentile; the portfolio effect scatters them from the 0th to the 81st.

chart.title: Where each planted group ranks (higher = found)
